question.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/fc06a4e63f38a315dd3944f65f871cca2dbdddee26ec268e857f79e5f4ab8848.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)$ is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

As $x$ increases to $\infty ,$ the graph tends to $y=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\infty }\operatorname{tan}⁡(4\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(2\pi ) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
